findings.title: Two statements say the 51 D-106 fixtures carry no producer role at all; the operative producers.rule and failsIf carve out an exception licensing them as the producer of the three authored-exact-bytes keys. The exception contradicts the artifact's own denial that it authors a corpus-to-map join, and the join it licenses is unestablished.
whereTheContradictionIs: whatThe51FixturesCover: 'They are not fixtureMemberMap keys. They carry no producer standing.' — unqualified, no exception.
executesWhenRun: 'The 51 D-106 fixtures remain FG-3 class evidence and are not executed as map-key producers.' — unqualified, no exception.
doesNot: 'Does not author a join between D-106 corpus ids and v14 fixtureMemberMap keys.' — unqualified denial.

closedMap.producedRidelessSchemaDerived.producers.rule: 'The 51 D-106 fixtures are not that producer except where v14 itself records authored-exact-bytes.' — the grammatical subject is the 51 fixtures and the exception attaches to them, licensing them as producer for TC-BYTE-EXACT.2, TC-NAME.4.after and TC-NAME.4.inside.

failsIf: 'the 51 D-106 fixtures are treated as fixtureMemberMap keys or as the producer of a key whose v14 producer is not authored-exact-bytes.' — this is the operative pass rule, and by naming only the not-authored-exact-bytes case as a failure it permits the other case. A failsIf carve-out is a permission, not a description.

whyTheLicensedJoinIsUnestablished.namespaces: The 51 corpus ids and the 80 map keys do not intersect at all, re-confirmed on live bytes. corpus v6's entries carry only the fields class, expected, id, path and sha256 — there is no memberKey, fixtureMemberMap or mapKey field anywhere in the file, and the tokens TC-NAME.4 and TC-BYTE-EXACT.2 occur zero times in it. No artifact records a join.
whyTheLicensedJoinIsUnestablished.expectedTokensDisagree: Even the closest candidates do not line up. Live map key TC-NAME.4.inside carries expected ACCEPT while the nearest corpus entry TC-NAME.stale-alias-inside-window carries expected RESOLVE. Live map key TC-NAME.4.after carries expected refuse:RJ-2 while corpus TC-NAME.stale-alias-after-window carries expected 'typed non-resolve'. v14's fixtureMemberMap.expectedOutcomeRule requires exactly one expected token per key, so a join would have to reconcile these, and none does.
whyTheLicensedJoinIsUnestablished.corpusStanding: component-manifest-fixture-corpus.v6.json is itself status CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, reviewStatus AWAITING-SATISFIED-GRADE-REVIEW, sealRecommendation DO-NOT-SEAL, binds NOTHING, with authorityClaim 'NONE ... Not SATISFIED.' Licensing it as the producer of three map keys rests a produced standing on an unaccepted artifact.
whyTheLicensedJoinIsUnestablished.contractGuards: v14 FG-4 states 'This artifact does not inherit any corpus verdict and does not close ID-DEP-8 by citing a file', and ID-DEP-P8 states that citing a corpus 'does not SATISFY DR-103 or close ID-DEP-8'. The exception closes part of the production question for three keys by citing a file.

findings.operativeBite: Under the twelve-report unit this specification pins, those three keys carry 3 x 12 = 36 member standings. Whether their bytes come from the D-106 corpus or from separately authored and reviewed bytes is left undetermined: two sentences forbid the corpus outright and two permit it. Whichever way an implementer reads it, one of the four statements is false, and on the permissive reading the produced standing rests on an identification that no artifact records and whose expected tokens disagree for two of the three keys. v14's coverage shape calls alternative producers report-invalid and FG-6 rejects a coverage array that 'records a producer/ride other than fixtureMemberMap.members[memberKey]'. This is the same producer surface as CLAUDE-G15H-V5-SF1, narrowed from 45 keys to 3 but not closed.
notRescuedBy: The producer enumeration does not rescue it. closedMap correctly records authored-exact-bytes as the producer for those three keys, which is a producer CATEGORY. Naming the category is right; identifying the category with these particular 51 files is the step that is neither necessary nor established.
The narrowness does not rescue it. The exception sits in failsIf, which is where this artifact states what makes a run fail, and it is the only place the corpus is given any production role at all.
doesNot does not rescue it. 'Does not author a join between D-106 corpus ids and v14 fixtureMemberMap keys' is the sentence the exception contradicts, not a sentence that limits it.
findings.remedyShape: Delete the exception and make the four statements agree. producers.rule should read that each key is produced by exactly the producer v14 records, that FG-6 rejects any other, and that the 51 D-106 fixtures are FG-3 class evidence and are not the producer of any map key; the failsIf line should read '... or as the producer of any fixtureMemberMap key', matching whatThe51FixturesCover and executesWhenRun. The three authored-exact-bytes keys are then produced by bytes authored and independently reviewed for those keys, which is what the producer category names and what a later cycle would supply. If a join to the D-106 corpus is genuinely intended, it has to be authored and independently reviewed as its own act, with the RESOLVE-versus-ACCEPT and typed-non-resolve-versus-RJ-2 token differences reconciled. This reviewer authors no join, reconciles no tokens, and writes no obligation text.
findings.gradeRationale: Graded SHOULD-FIX and not a blocker because the artifact binds nothing, applies nothing, is CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED at DO-NOT-SEAL with gates2and3HoldForDR103 false, and because the producer enumeration it delivers is exhaustively correct. Graded SHOULD-FIX and not advisory because the clause sits in an operative pass rule, contradicts three unqualified statements including the artifact's own denial, and licenses a produced standing on an unaccepted artifact through an identification nothing records.

decision.recommendation: DO-NOT-SEAL. Do not record. The closedMap and the producer enumeration are exhaustively correct and should be kept verbatim. A v7 that deletes the authored-exact-bytes exception from producers.rule and from the failsIf line, so that all four statements about the 51 D-106 fixtures agree, would on these bytes carry no remaining finding known to this reviewer.
decision.summaryForCoordinator: v6 lands CLAUDE-G15H-V5-SF1. The false v5 identity between the 51 corpus fixtures and the 48 map keys is replaced by a correct FG-3 class-evidence claim, and the per-key producers are now enumerated and verified exhaustively against live v14 in both directions — fixtureGenerator 31, S-3-EMIT 8, behavioral-harness 6, authored-exact-bytes 3, zero mismatches, union equal to the 48 keys, arithmetic correct. V1-SF1 through V4-SF1 all remain landed, with the closedMap 80-key union still set-equal to live and all ten rided keys' rides and expected tokens byte-exact. Every mechanical check is clean — subject unmoved at 5ada9d37 and 0444, fifteen of fifteen cited digests equal live bytes, file 08 pin equal to live, HEAD 5d5d778, required-now 26, thirty gate rows, all three cells at 80 of 80 map keys, prohibition scan clean. One SHOULD-FIX stands: producers.rule and the failsIf line carve out an exception permitting the 51 D-106 fixtures to be the producer of the three authored-exact-bytes keys, while whatThe51FixturesCover, executesWhenRun and doesNot each say without qualification that they carry no producer role and that no corpus-to-map join is authored. The permitted join is unestablished — zero namespace overlap, no join field in corpus v6, expected tokens that disagree for two of the three keys, and a corpus that is itself CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED and AWAITING-SATISFIED-GRADE-REVIEW.
